title: MasRouter: Learning to Route LLMs for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper introduces MasRouter, a high-performing, cost-effective, and inductive Multi-Agent System Router that balances effectiveness and efficiency by determining collaboration modes, allocating agent roles, and routing LLMs through a cascaded controller network.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're working on a complex project with multiple team members, each with their own expertise. You need to assign tasks efficiently and choose the right tools for each task. This is similar to Multi-Agent System Routing (MASR), where we need to route LLMs to agents in a multi-agent system to balance performance and cost.

MasRouter is designed to solve this problem by integrating collaboration mode determination, role allocation, and LLM routing into a unified framework.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
MasRouter employs a cascaded controller network to construct a multi-agent system that balances effectiveness and efficiency. The network consists of three components: collaboration mode determiner, role allocator, and LLM router. Each component is designed to optimize the trade-off between performance and cost.

For example, the collaboration mode determiner uses a variational latent variable model to route the user query to a suitable collaboration module.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Extensive experiments demonstrate that MasRouter is high-performing, achieving a 1.8% ∼ 8.2% improvement over the state-of-the-art method on MBPP, and economical, reducing overhead by up to 52.07% compared to SOTA methods on HumanEval.

The results show that MasRouter can seamlessly integrate with mainstream multi-agent systems, reducing overhead by 17.21% ∼ 28.17% via customized routing.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The availability of a routing method for multi-agent systems is even more essential than for single-agent systems. Multi-agent systems have been proven to outperform single-agent approaches significantly, but they often incur substantial costs and face challenges in dynamic LLM selection.

MasRouter addresses this gap by providing a high-performing, cost-effective, and inductive MASR solution that can be applied to various tasks and domains.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
MasRouter introduces several key innovations, including a cascaded controller network that integrates collaboration mode determination, role allocation, and LLM routing, and a variational latent variable model for collaboration mode determination.

These innovations enable MasRouter to construct a multi-agent system that balances effectiveness and efficiency, making it a valuable tool for various applications.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To demonstrate the effectiveness of MasRouter, we provide a simple example of how to apply it to a physics problem. The problem involves determining the constant speed at which a motor can lift a 6 kg mass.

By using MasRouter, we can assign roles to agents and route LLMs to each agent, enabling collaborative reasoning and calculation.
